messages:
maya: quick Q — noticed a pile of debug snapshots in s3://redwood-debug-dumps/session-exports/ that are older than 90 days. retention says 90d for debug dumps, right? any reason we shouldn't prune?
sam: which prefix exactly? are these customer payloads or internal traces?
maya: prefix is session-exports/* — some files look like full request/response dumps and include request bodies. example to list: ```aws s3 ls s3://redwood-debug-dumps/session-exports/ --recursive | sort -r | head -n 50```
security-bot: Retention policy summary: debug-dumps/session-exports = 90 days, traces/* = 180 days. See runbook: https://runbooks.internal/retention (automated notice)
jordan: infra note — we had a bucket migration last quarter and the lifecycle rule didn't get applied to the session-exports prefix. I'm fine with backfilling deletes, but if these contain PII we need compliance scrub first.
lina: @maya thanks for the callout. Policy: anything with customer-identifying data must be scrubbed before bulk deletion. Non-PII artifacts older than 90d are ok to delete. Please run the scrub dry-run: `bin/log-scrub --bucket redwood-debug-dumps --prefix session-exports/ --dry-run` and share samples. If the scrub flags PII, we escalate to the data-retention board.
maya: running dry-run now, will paste results shortly.
maya: dry-run results: 73 objects flagged that contain JSON request bodies; 12 of those include fields like `email` or `ssn` (sample key: session-exports/2025-11-03/abc123.json). I'm moving the flagged list to #incidents-private per policy and will attach a short ticket. cc @lina @jordan
lina: ok — compliance approves scrub + delete after scrub finishes. Please open an internal ticket with the list and tag security+compliance. Once scrubbed, lifecycle delete is approved. :thumbsup:
jordan: I'll patch the lifecycle rule to include session-exports/ and queue a weekly scrub job to scan for PII and then allow S3 lifecycle to remove objects older than 90d. Plan to run backfill + delete today EOD unless anyone objects.
sam: :thumbsup: no objections, thanks all.
